messages.author: b2e826fb9bf94df2
messages.subject: Error with read.myacc.csv:  data[, params_rawdata[["rmc.col.temp"]]] :    subscript out of bounds
parts:
Dear all, 

I am trying to use the read.myacc.csv function to run a .csv into GGIR. I have had no trouble with the test run of read.myacc.csv, but when I incorporate into GGIR, I consistently get the following error: 

Investigate calibration of the sensors with function g.calibrate:

Loading chunk: 1Error in data[, params_rawdata[["rmc.col.temp"]]] :
  subscript out of bounds

It seems to not be able to find my col.temp? Although it works fine in the test of read.myacc.csv and locates the temp column just fine. The only thing that allowed me to run my .csv through GGIR was deleting the two lines of code that refer to temperature, thus prompting GGIR to think there is no temperature data in my .csv and I assume use default temp values. 

How can I fix this issue? Or is it necessary to fix? My temperature for all timepoints is 28.5 C and I am unsure if removing temp has any impact. Below is my code from GGIR. The only way to run it without receiving the error was to remove the lines 
"rmc.col.temp = 5 and rmc.unit.temp = "C", preventing it from seeing temp altogether. I have also messed with rearranging the order of columns, as well as exporting my .csv in different ways, and so far nothing works except for getting rid of temperature.

Thank you for your help. 

Best,
Joanna

GGIR(
  mode=c(1:5),
  datadir="/Users/joanna/Pa_Lab/LearnIT_July2023/two_sub/sub_133_97_102.csv",
  outputdir="/Users/joanna/Pa_Lab/LearnIT_July2023/two_sub/output_102_2",
  studyname = "test",
  f0=1, f1=1, # change f1 if you want to run multiple subjects at once
  #------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Part 1: reading file, auto-calibration, and extracting features
  # read.myacc.csv arguments
                 rmc.nrow = Inf,
                 rmc.dec = ".",
                 rmc.firstrow.acc = 1,
                 rmc.col.acc = 2:4,
                 rmc.col.time= 1,
                 rmc.unit.acc = "g",
                 rmc.unit.time = "POSIX",
                 rmc.format.time = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS",
                 rmc.sf = 10.0, # 10 hz = 10 samples per second
                 rmc.check4timegaps = FALSE,
                 desiredtz = "America/Los_Angeles",
                 configtz = "America/Los_Angeles",
  do.enmo = TRUE,             do.anglez=TRUE,
  chunksize=1,                printsummary=TRUE,
  idloc=2, #id is located in the filename
  #------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

On Friday, 17 November 2023 at 12:49 AM, joeck...@gmail.com <joeck...@gmail.com> wrote:

Dear all,

I am trying to use the read.myacc.csv function to run a .csv into GGIR. I have had no trouble with the test run of read.myacc.csv, but when I incorporate into GGIR, I consistently get the following error:

Investigate calibration of the sensors with function g.calibrate:

Loading chunk: 1Error in data[, params_rawdata[["rmc.col.temp"]]] :
subscript out of bounds

It seems to not be able to find my col.temp? Although it works fine in the test of read.myacc.csv and locates the temp column just fine. The only thing that allowed me to run my .csv through GGIR was deleting the two lines of code that refer to temperature, thus prompting GGIR to think there is no temperature data in my .csv and I assume use default temp values.

How can I fix this issue? Or is it necessary to fix? My temperature for all timepoints is 28.5 C and I am unsure if removing temp has any impact. Below is my code from GGIR. The only way to run it without receiving the error was to remove the lines
"rmc.col.temp = 5 and rmc.unit.temp = "C", preventing it from seeing temp altogether. I have also messed with rearranging the order of columns, as well as exporting my .csv in different ways, and so far nothing works except for getting rid of temperature.

Thank you for your help.

Best,
Joanna

GGIR(
mode=c(1:5),
datadir="/Users/joanna/Pa_Lab/LearnIT_July2023/two_sub/sub_133_97_102.csv",
outputdir="/Users/joanna/Pa_Lab/LearnIT_July2023/two_sub/output_102_2",
studyname = "test",
f0=1, f1=1, # change f1 if you want to run multiple subjects at once
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Part 1: reading file, auto-calibration, and extracting features
# read.myacc.csv arguments
rmc.nrow = Inf,
rmc.dec = ".",
rmc.firstrow.acc = 1,
rmc.col.acc = 2:4,
rmc.col.time= 1,
rmc.unit.acc = "g",
rmc.unit.time = "POSIX",
rmc.format.time = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS",
rmc.sf = 10.0, # 10 hz = 10 samples per second
rmc.check4timegaps = FALSE,
desiredtz = "America/Los_Angeles",
configtz = "America/Los_Angeles",
do.enmo = TRUE, do.anglez=TRUE,
chunksize=1, printsummary=TRUE,
idloc=2, #id is located in the filename
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
